parts.visual:
When your product becomes globally successful, criminals will manufacture exact, cheap copies of it. This is the Counterfeit market.

The Threat:
1. Revenue Loss: They steal your sales.
2. Brand Destruction: A consumer buys a fake version, it breaks instantly, and they blame your brand on social media.
3. The Whack-a-Mole Problem: If you sue a counterfeiter in Asia, they close the factory on Monday and open a new one on Tuesday.
parts.audio: Counterfeiters manufacture cheap, illegal copies of your successful products. They steal your revenue and destroy your brand reputation when their cheap fakes inevitably break.

questions.question: Your luxury watch brand is being counterfeited. The fakes are so good that only an expert can tell the difference. What is the true danger to your company?
options: Brand Dilution. If everyone on the street is wearing a $50 fake version of your watch, the wealthy clients will stop buying the real $10,000 version because it is no longer 'exclusive'.
questions.correct_answer: Brand Dilution. If everyone on the street is wearing a $50 fake version of your watch, the wealthy clients will stop buying the real $10,000 version because it is no longer 'exclusive'.
questions.explanation: Luxury brands sell exclusivity. Counterfeits destroy exclusivity.

questions.question: Listen to the Head of Global Security. What strategy are they using against the counterfeiters?
questions.tts_text: We cannot arrest all the factories in China. Instead, we are using AI to instantly identify and delete their listings on Amazon and Alibaba. We are cutting off their distribution.
questions.explanation: The 'Whack-a-Mole' reality means you cannot stop production. You must stop their ability to sell to western consumers on digital platforms.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'Counterfeit' and a 'Grey Market' good?
options: A counterfeit is a fake product. A grey market good is a real, authentic product that is imported and sold illegally by an unauthorized dealer, undercutting your official prices.
Grey market goods are painted grey.
questions.correct_answer: A counterfeit is a fake product. A grey market good is a real, authentic product that is imported and sold illegally by an unauthorized dealer, undercutting your official prices.
questions.explanation: Grey markets destroy your global pricing strategy (e.g., someone buying your product cheap in India and reselling it in London).

questions.question: How do modern brands use 'Supply Chain Tech' to fight fakes?
options: By embedding NFC microchips or blockchain-verified QR codes directly into the physical product, allowing the consumer to instantly verify its authenticity with their phone.
questions.correct_answer: By embedding NFC microchips or blockchain-verified QR codes directly into the physical product, allowing the consumer to instantly verify its authenticity with their phone.
questions.explanation: Technology is the only scalable defense against global counterfeiting rings.
